evidence: Dry-run `patch -p1` of patch.diff onto a scratch copy of base applies all 7 files cleanly; the applied copy is identical to generated/ (diff -rq empty). No tests were run.
checks.json: patch_applies=true, commands=[], api_inspection=[].
patch.diff removes only Segment yields in underline_bar.py (the zero-width and piece yields) and the Opacity yield in opacity.py:36-41. No test lines are removed; both test diffs are additive.
generated/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:1 is a new module at the same path as reference/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py.
generated/src/textual/renderables/underline_bar.py:23-34 puts clickable_ranges in the UnderlineBar renderable, matching reference/src/textual/renderables/underline_bar.py:23-29.
generated/src/textual/_layout_resolve.py:22-34 places EdgeSpec beside the existing Edge protocol.
generated/docs/reference/tabs.md contains `::: textual.widgets.tabs.Tabs`, matching the base docs/reference/app.md:1 convention (no heading).
Tabs.__init__ at generated/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:233-247 keeps the reference parameter names and order (reference/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:199-211) and adds a trailing `name` parameter.

Public methods match reference names and semantics: find_tab_by_name (tabs.py:269), activate_next_tab (283), activate_previous_tab (288), activate_tab_by_first_char (293), activate_tab_by_number (316), action_range_clicked (337).
UnderlineBar keeps the positional slot for clickable_ranges before width (underline_bar.py:23-28), matching the reference signature.

Deviation: TabsRenderable (tabs.py:80-91) takes positional `bar_position` and has no `width`, whereas reference/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:48-61 is keyword-only with `bar_offset` and `width`. TabsRenderable is not in `__all__` (tabs.py:401), so it is an internal render helper rather than a public contract.
criteria.deficiency: No blocking deficiency. Minor: TabsRenderable's signature differs from the reference (bar_offset renamed to bar_position, width dropped, keyword-only became positional). It is not exported, so it does not break the public API.

evidence: generated/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:12-18 imports only lower-level modules (events, _layout_resolve, keys, reactive, renderables.opacity, renderables.underline_bar, widget), mirroring the reference imports at reference/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:12-21.
No core module imports from widgets/ in the patch.
action_range_clicked (tabs.py:337) handles the `range_clicked(...)` meta emitted at tabs.py:152 and by UnderlineBar at underline_bar.py:92-97.
watch__active_tab_name (tabs.py:374) follows the watch_<reactive> convention used by the base Reactive (reactive.py check_watchers).
Tabs is not added to widgets/__init__.py, the same as the reference, which does not modify that file.
EdgeSpec satisfies the existing Edge protocol structurally (_layout_resolve.py:22-34), so layout_resolve accepts it without any registration.
_layout_resolve.py:4 adds `from dataclasses import dataclass`, which is stdlib.
tabs.py imports only rich (already a dependency) and textual internals. The patch does not touch pyproject.toml.
Tab layout and rendering live in TabsRenderable (generated/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:65-195); state, keys, and animation live in Tabs (tabs.py:197-392).

Click spans are emitted by the renderable (underline_bar.py:92-97), and the blend fix that keeps the rest of the segment style is in opacity.py:36-41. This matches the reference split (reference underline_bar.py:91, opacity.py:36).
Reuses the existing layout_resolve via EdgeSpec (tabs.py:120 `sizes = iter(layout_resolve(width, edges))`) instead of a parallel layout path.
Reuses the existing Opacity renderable (tabs.py:155), the Reactive + animate mechanism (tabs.py:374-385), and the existing UnderlineBar.

The base Edge protocol is left unchanged. Dock and grid layouts (layouts/dock.py:106, layouts/grid.py:290) keep working unchanged. The reference instead converts Edge into a NamedTuple; the candidate's approach is a valid alternative.

UnderlineBar stays generic: clickable_ranges is a name-to-span mapping with action meta applied in the renderable (underline_bar.py:23-34, 91-97), the same mechanism as the reference (reference underline_bar.py:91).
Tabs keeps the widget/action boundary: it exposes action_range_clicked (tabs.py:337) and does not reach into app internals beyond self.app.set_focus (tabs.py:364).
Relative imports in the widgets package match base widgets/_header.py (`from .. import events`, `from ..widget import Widget`).
`async def on_key` (tabs.py:345) and `await self.app.set_focus(None)` (tabs.py:364) match base async handlers (widget.py:356) and the async set_focus (app.py:306).

Google-style docstrings match the base style. Tests are appended to tests/renderables/test_underline_bar.py (additive hunks) and added as tests/test_tabs.py using tests.utilities.render, as the base tests do.
Label row with auto or fixed padding: tabs.py:102-120. Click ranges per tab: tabs.py:137-138. Bar interpolation: tabs.py:170-195.

Digit keys with 0 meaning the 10th tab or the last tab: tabs.py:316-335. Next/previous with wrap: tabs.py:283-292. First-character search after the active tab with wrap, never selecting the active tab: tabs.py:293-314.
Inactive text dimmed via Opacity and given a click meta: tabs.py:147-156. Bar animates to the new position: tabs.py:374-385. Zero-width bar path: underline_bar.py:55.

Where the candidate departs from the reference, the candidate is correct. (1) reference/src/textual/widgets/tabs.py:140-145 advances the cursor before computing the selection span, so for a tab with lpad=2, label=4, rpad=2 it yields (6,14) rather than the tab's own span (0,8). The candidate's tabs.py:137-138 yields (0,8). (2) reference tabs.py:248 calls self.app.set_focus(None) without await, although app.py:306 is async, so Escape would never defocus; the candidate awaits (tabs.py:364). (3) reference tabs.py:255 passes multi-character key names such as 'up' to first-char search; the candidate restricts it to single characters (tabs.py:371).
criteria.deficiency: No blocking deficiency. Not carried over: the reference's sandbox/tabs.py demo, the dev_sandbox example move, and cosmetic edits to _header.py and _event_broker.py. None of these is a behavioral requirement.
